title: Observability and Production Reliability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Observability and Production Reliability”?
options: Observability and Production Reliability should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Observability and Production Reliability helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Observability and Production Reliability means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Observability and Production Reliability removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Observability and Production Reliability helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Observability and Production Reliability is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Structured frontend logging” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Structured frontend logging” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Structured frontend logging” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Structured frontend logging” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Structured frontend logging” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Structured frontend logging” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Structured frontend logging” under Observability and Production Reliability. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Observability and Production Reliability”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
